column3: A giant market with a tall tower in Urumqi, selling carpets, dried fruit, nuts, knives, musical instruments and silk, in the style of a Central Asian bazaar.

column1: 新疆维吾尔自治区博物馆
column3: A museum that holds mummies from the Tarim Basin, including the Loulan Beauty, along with Silk Road treasures and local peoples' costumes.
A deep blue mountain lake under snow-capped peaks and forests of spruce, with a calm surface that mirrors the mountains. It is a classic Xinjiang view.
A mountain pasture where Kazakh herders keep horses and sheep, with green meadows, pine forests and felt tents in summer.
Chicken, potatoes and peppers in a spicy sauce, served on a big plate with wide belt noodles. A hearty dish that was born in Xinjiang in the 1980s.
Chunks of lamb on skewers, grilled over charcoal and dusted with cumin and chili, the smell of every Xinjiang evening.
Polo is rice cooked with lamb, carrots and raisins in a big pot, a festive and filling dish of Uyghur cuisine.
A round baked bread with a crisp, golden crust, made in a clay oven. Naan is eaten at every meal, and some are as big as a plate.
Laghman is hand-pulled noodles served with a stir-fried topping of meat and vegetables, a Xinjiang staple.
Samsa are baked pastries filled with lamb and onion, with a crisp, flaky crust, and are sold hot from the oven.
Meat roasted in the naan oven, a deep pit of clay, so that it is tender, juicy and rich.
Turpan raisins come in many colors, from green to black, and are dried in airy brick houses in the dry desert wind.
Hami melons have orange flesh and a very sweet taste, grown in the oases of eastern Xinjiang, and once a tribute to emperors.
A huge set of songs, music and dance of the Uyghur people, with twelve main suites that take about 24 hours to perform in full. It is on UNESCO's list.
Atlas silk is a cloth dyed in bold, bright, blurred patterns, woven by Uyghur craftspeople in Hotan.
A gathering with music, dance, songs, games and food, where the whole community joins in.
The Uyghur art of tightrope walking, in which performers walk on a rope high above the ground, with little more than a balancing pole.
A red sandstone ridge that seems to burn in the heat of the desert sun, known from the novel Journey to the West.
A green valley of vineyards in the desert, with grape trellises, shady paths and a sweet harvest in late summer.
An ancient city built on a river island, with remains of streets and temples, left in the desert since the 14th century.
The remains of a Silk Road city of the Gaochang kingdom, where the monk Xuanzang stayed on his way to India.
A minaret built of mud brick in the 18th century with patterns of bricks, a landmark of Turpan.
A dry salt lake with a salty crust, the lowest point in China, about 154 meters below sea level.
A canyon village with old Buddhist caves and a traditional Uyghur settlement of mud houses.
A whole lamb roasted in the oven, served on a large platter at feasts and celebrations.
Seedless grapes in many varieties, grown in the hot desert oasis under long sunlight, and sold fresh or dried.
One of the largest mosques in China, standing on the main square of Kashgar, with a bright yellow front and tall minarets. Thousands pray here on Fridays.
A maze of mud-brick houses and narrow lanes in Kashgar, with craftsmen's workshops and teahouses.
A tomb complex with green tiles and domes, where several generations of a Uyghur family are buried, and linked by legend to a Qing imperial concubine.
A weekly market in Kashgar where farmers, herders and traders meet to buy and sell livestock, spices, cloth and food.
A high snow peak in the Pamirs, called the Father of Ice Mountains, with a broad, rounded dome that is more than 7,500 meters high.
A lake at the foot of the Pamirs, with a very blue color against white mountains, where Kyrgyz herders graze their yaks.
Lamb on skewers from Kashgar, grilled over charcoal and sprinkled with cumin and salt.
A thick yogurt served with honey or sugar, a popular dessert on Kashgar's streets.
A block of walnuts, almonds, raisins and dried fruit set in sugar syrup, and sliced by weight to order.
The rawap is a Uyghur long-necked lute with a carved body and skin top, with a lively, sharp tone.
In early summer, the fields around Yining turn purple with lavender, and the air is filled with its scent.
A big blue lake high in the mountains, surrounded by meadows, often called the last tear of the Atlantic.
A grassland at the foot of the Tianshan, with rolling green hills, spruce forests and herds of horses and sheep.
A high alpine meadow with wide views, wildflowers and Kazakh herders' tents in summer.
Fermented mare's milk, mildly sour and slightly fizzy, a traditional Kazakh drink.
Buns filled with lamb and onion, with a thin skin so that you can see the filling, steamed until juicy.
The dombra is a Kazakh two-stringed lute, used to accompany songs and stories on the steppe.
A lake whose color changes from green to blue with the seasons, among forests and peaks in the Altai Mountains. In autumn, the trees turn gold.
A wooden village of Tuvan people with log cabins, smoke rising from chimneys and golden larches in autumn.
A mining town and gorge of rock and rivers in the Altai, known for rare minerals and wild scenery.
Salty milk tea of the Kazakhs, served with bread and butter, and a warm welcome for guests.
Boiled lamb with noodles, eaten by hand, a Kazakh feast.
Fish from the cold, clear rivers and lakes of the Altai, often grilled or stewed.
A small people who live in the Kanas area, with their own language and customs, known for their log houses and their music.
Some of the earliest Buddhist cave paintings in China, in a cliff above a river, with murals in colors from the Silk Road.
A giant naan, as large as a table top, baked in Kuqa and often shared among a family.
A small, sweet white apricot from Kuqa, which ripens in early summer and is soft and juicy.
Large, sweet jujubes from Hotan, dried in the desert sun, a popular snack and gift.
Hotan's walnuts have thin shells and a rich, creamy kernel, grown in old orchards.
The largest inland freshwater lake in China, with reeds, birds and a desert shore, a popular destination.
A sweet and juicy pear with a thin skin and a fragrance, grown near Korla and well known across China.
Crisp, sweet apples with a bright color, grown in the sunny, dry Aksu region.
Hami grapes are sweet and juicy and grown in the dry climate of eastern Xinjiang.
Grilled meat from the oil city of Karamay, a favorite with workers and visitors.
A hearty noodle dish of hand-pulled noodles with a rich stir-fried topping.
Grapes grown by settlers on the oasis of Shihezi, a green city in the desert, which are sweet and juicy.
